news.head: S&P 500 falls 2% for a sixth straight loss; Dow drops below 50,000
news.srcN: Capp Notes, Nov 19; AP via WPTF, Nov 19
news.mean: The S&P 500 closed at 7,175.83 (-2.02%), its sixth straight loss and longest streak since 2024, about 8.2% below October's record. The Dow lost 2.19% to 49,097 (first close under 50,000 since June, 1 of 30 components up) and the Nasdaq 2.25% to 23,879. Decliners beat advancers 464 to 37 and all 11 sectors fell; the VIX jumped 15.8% to 28.44.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Breadth was nearly one-sided, so Friday's Waller and Cook speeches and the Michigan sentiment print may set the tone.
news.later: Investors may watch whether the selloff turns into a broader valuation reset or a bounce; this week is Dow -6.2%, S&P about -5%.

news.head: Nvidia beats and guides higher, but the CEO resigns and the stock falls
news.srcN: Constellation Research, Nov 17; Capp Notes, Nov 19
news.mean: Nvidia reported Q3 FY27 revenue of $115.8B (+103%) versus $108.7B expected, EPS $2.70 versus $2.47, and guided Q4 revenue to about $130B versus $124.9B expected, with an extra $150B buyback. CEO Jensen Huang resigned and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The stock closed -3.30% at $145.98 and was down about 1.9% premarket Nov 20, its lowest in over a year.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Watch Nvidia's premarket low and whether AI names stabilize.
news.later: Investors may separate the strong fundamentals from the governance and sentiment shock.

news.head: Anthropic's record IPO opens at $111.50 but closes at $97.17
news.srcN: Wall Street Republic, Nov 19; conservativedailynews, Nov 20
news.mean: Anthropic priced at $83 (above range), raised $81.3B in the largest IPO on record, opened at $111.50, hit $115.10 and closed at $97.17 (+17.07% versus the IPO price, -12.85% from the first trade), valuing it near $1.75T. It traded about 6% lower premarket Nov 20.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Volatility is likely high in the first sessions of a new listing.
news.later: IPO supply and size can drain cash from other growth names.

news.head: Fed December hike near fully priced; Philadelphia Fed's Paulson says more hikes needed
news.mean: CME FedWatch showed 96.4% for a 25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC (Kalshi 89.3%); another outlet cited 98.4%. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said the Fed will need to raise rates again, and Saxo says money markets price at least two more hikes by mid-2027.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Fed Gov. Waller speaks 8:25am ET and Cook at 12:15pm ET Friday.
news.later: Investors may plan for a higher-for-longer path through mid-2027.

news.mean: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate averaged 7.28%, up 17bp from 7.11% a week earlier and versus 6.26% a year ago; the 15-year was 6.66% versus 6.45%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Homebuilders may stay sensitive to the 10-year yield.
news.later: Affordability remains a drag on housing demand.

news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.

news.mean: Intuit fell about 10-11% after hours on weak fiscal 2027 guidance and agreed to sell Mailchimp at a $3.68B enterprise value. Full results were not itemized in the sources.

news.head: Walmart raises its outlook; off-price TJX jumped earlier in the week
news.mean: Walmart reported Q3 revenue of $188.8B (+5.2%) and adjusted EPS $0.65, with US comps +2.9% versus 3.1% expected, and raised FY EPS guidance to $2.84-2.89; the stock fell 1.04% to $126.04. Williams-Sonoma fell 15.16% to $220.66 and Ross Stores fell about 7% after hours.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Watch Ross and Williams-Sonoma for the home and apparel read.
news.later: Retail results are mixed, with share gains at value retailers.

news.head: AMD falls 7.7% after a short report on China ties
news.mean: AMD fell 7.72% to $489.19 after a Hunterbrook short report on China ties, which AMD denied. Palo Alto rose 6.4% on its beat, and PDD rose 11% despite a revenue miss.
react: Beat and Applied Compute purchase for $4.5B
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Short-report moves often fade or extend within days.
news.later: Investors may wait for AMD's reply to be tested.

news.head: Asia heads for its worst week since 2020 as the AI selloff spreads
news.mean: The Nikkei fell 5.06% to 56,436.65 and the Kospi 5.21%, with Taiwan down over 6%; MSCI Asia ex-Japan is down 8% on the week, its worst since March 2020. Drivers cited were Huang's departure, slower data-center construction and the AMD report; Deutsche Bank called it 'very oversold'. Nasdaq-100 futures were -1.1% premarket.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: broad, one-day selloffs on heavy breadth often see sharp rebounds or further drops depending on the next catalyst, not a fixed pattern.
news.today: Overseas weakness points to a soft open.
news.later: Extreme readings (CNN Fear & Greed 19) can precede bounces, but not reliably.

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
